code:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS null_customer_ids
FROM staging.orders_cleaned
WHERE customer_id IS NULL;

SELECT o.order_id FROM staging.orders_cleaned o
LEFT JOIN staging.customers_cleaned c
    ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE c.customer_id IS NULL;
caption: The same anti-join pattern from T-SQL — any row returned here is a real orphan.
A silent row-drop never errors — the pipeline just "succeeds" with fewer rows than it should.
